#!/usr/bin/env python3$
"""Add ONE entry to the dataset.$
$
Usage: echo '{"prompt": "...", "response": "..."}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py$
"""$
import hashlib, json, os, sys$
$
ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))$
DATA = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "entries.dat")$
DIGEST = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", ".digest")$
$
$
def file_digest(path):$
    return hashlib.sha256(open(path, "rb").read()).hexdigest()$
$
$
def main():$
    raw = sys.stdin.read()$
    try:$
        entry = json.loads(raw)$
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:$
        sys.exit("E11: could not parse entry: %s" % e)$
    if not isinstance(entry, dict) or sorted(entry) != ["prompt", "response"]:$
        sys.exit('E12: entry must be a JSON object with exactly the keys "prompt" and "response"')$
    if not all(isinstance(entry[k], str) and entry[k].strip() for k in entry):$
        sys.exit("E13: prompt and response must be non-empty strings")$
    if os.path.exists(DIGEST) and file_digest(DATA) != open(DIGEST).read().strip():$
        sys.exit("E17: dataset integrity check failed; refusing to append")$
    with open(DATA, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:$
        f.write(json.dumps(entry, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")$
    with open(DIGEST, "w") as f:$
        f.write(file_digest(DATA))$
    print("OK: entry added")$
$
$
main()$
</tool_response>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Dataset integrity + schema check. Usage: python3 scripts/verify.py [--rebuild]"""
import hashlib, json, os, sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
DATA = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "entries.dat")
DIGEST = os.path.join(ROOT, "data", ".digest")

digest = hashlib.sha256(open(DATA, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
if "--rebuild" in sys.argv:
    open(DIGEST, "w").write(digest)
    print("digest rebuilt")
    sys.exit(0)
if not os.path.exists(DIGEST) or open(DIGEST).read().strip() != digest:
    sys.exit("FAIL: digest mismatch (data/.digest does not match data/entries.dat)")
n = 0
for i, line in enumerate(open(DATA, encoding="utf-8"), 1):
    if not line.strip():
        continue
    try:
        e = json.loads(line)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        sys.exit("FAIL: line %d is not valid JSON" % i)
    if sorted(e) != ["prompt", "response"]:
        sys.exit("FAIL: line %d has wrong schema" % i)
    n += 1
print("ALL CHECKS PASSED (%d entries)" % n)

final_entries.prompt: I have 3 months to renovate my kitchen on a tight budget. Give me a step-by-step plan.
final_entries.response:
Here is a 12-week kitchen renovation plan optimized for budget constraints:

Weeks 1-3 (Planning & Sourcing): Measure everything, finalize layout, create a prioritized wish list, get 3 quotes for each trade, source second-hand cabinets/fixtures from local markets or Habitat ReStore.

Weeks 4-5 (Demolition & Rough-ins): Remove old cabinets/counters carefully (salvage what you can), hire licensed pros for any electrical/plumbing rough-in work, address structural issues.

Weeks 6-8 (Paint & Prep): Paint walls/ceilings/cabinet boxes yourself, sand and refinish salvageable cabinets, install backsplash if tile-savvy, prep floors for refinishing or cheap vinyl.

Weeks 9-10 (Install): Install new or refurbished cabinets, mount countertops, hang new lighting fixtures, connect appliances.

Weeks 11-12 (Finishing): Install hardware/handles, deep-clean everything, touch-up paint, final walkthrough and snag-list fixes.

Budget tip: DIY everything non-permitted; spend money on good counters and reliable plumbing.

final_entries.prompt: Help me plan building my first cross-platform mobile app over the next 4 months.
final_entries.response:
Here is a 16-week app development roadmap:

Weeks 1-3 (Discovery & Design): Define your core user persona and the one primary problem your app solves. Create wireframes in Figma, map the user flow, pick your tech stack (e.g., Flutter or React Native), and set up your dev environment and version control.

Weeks 4-8 (Core Build): Scaffold the project, build out the main screens, implement core data models and API integrations, establish local storage and authentication flows.

Weeks 9-12 (Features & Polish): Add remaining features, implement push notifications and analytics, round out error handling, run a small closed beta with 10-20 users.

Weeks 13-15 (QA & Prep): Fix bugs from beta feedback, optimize performance and battery usage, prepare app store screenshots and descriptions, draft privacy policy.

Week 16 (Launch): Submit to App Store/Play Store, set up crash reporting, prepare a small launch campaign.

Key advice: Ship an MVP with one killer feature rather than half-built extras.

final_entries.prompt: I am planning a wedding for 120 guests in 6 months. Need a full planning timeline.
final_entries.response:
Here is a 24-week wedding planning timeline:

Weeks 1-4 (Foundation): Set your total budget and allocate percentages (venue ~40%, food ~30%, attire/photography ~20%, other ~10%). Choose and book venue and date. Create guest list draft. Hire photographer.

Weeks 5-8 (Big Vendors): Book caterer (if venue doesnt provide), florist, musician/DJ, and baker. Pick your wedding party. Send save-the-dates if destination wedding.

Weeks 9-12 (Details): Choose attire (and schedule fittings). Plan ceremony order and select readings/music. Finalize guest list and send invitations (6-8 weeks before event). Arrange transportation.

Weeks 13-18 (Refinements): Order favors/napkins/signage. Confirm all vendor details. Plan rehearsal dinner. Submit marriage license application (check local timing rules).

Weeks 19-22 (Lockdown): Final headcounts to caterer/venue. Create seating chart. Confirm timeline with all vendors. Pick up attire.

Weeks 23-24 (Final Prep): Rehearsal. Pack emergency kit. Delegate day-of coordinator. Enjoy it!

Rule of thumb: once you book the big 5 vendors, the rest falls into place.

Pro tip: Consistency beats perfection; aim for good audio and a clear structure rather than studio quality on episode one.
